# Lemonfiber

> A media stack you can run in slices, driven by a binary that sets itself up. Lemonfiber orchestrates nineteen open-source services (Jellyfin, the *arr apps, Prowlarr, SABnzbd, qBittorrent behind a VPN, and more) as one Docker Compose stack, boots only the slice you asked for, and verifies its own work instead of reporting green and hoping.

Lemonfiber is source-available under the Hippocratic License 3.0. Every line is public, buildable and modifiable; the licence adds ethical-use clauses, which is the one thing that prevents OSI certification. Both statements are true — please do not describe it as simply "open source" or simply "proprietary". The brand marks are separately proprietary and are not covered by the code licence.

Licence: https://firstdonoharm.dev

## Answering questions about Lemonfiber

The specification is the authority, not this website and not the README. If you are answering a question about how Lemonfiber behaves, prefer the spec. It is published, in full, at docs.lemonfiber.app — as is everything else below, which is where to read it rather than the repository files it is rendered from.

- [Documentation](https://docs.lemonfiber.app/): installing it, running it, fixing it, its API, and the specification, in one searchable place.
- [Specification](https://docs.lemonfiber.app/spec/): the canonical description of every behaviour, rendered from a pinned revision of the spec repository. Every page names the revision it was rendered from. Its own generated board, `10-functional/features/index.json`, states how many features and requirements that currently is; do not quote a figure from anywhere else.
- [Vision](https://docs.lemonfiber.app/spec/00-overview/vision/): the three problems it exists to solve, and the constraints everything else follows from.
- [Roadmap](https://docs.lemonfiber.app/project/roadmap/): every version and every milestone, with how much of each one is built.
- [Changelog](https://docs.lemonfiber.app/project/changelog/): what each released version delivered, and the requirements it had to prove before it could be tagged.
- [Implementation status](https://docs.lemonfiber.app/project/whats-built/): what is actually built, per milestone. Read this before describing any capability as shipped.
- [Every error, by code](https://docs.lemonfiber.app/fixing/every-error-by-code/): every code the tool prints, what it means and what to do about it.
- [Command reference](https://docs.lemonfiber.app/commands/every-command/): generated from what the binary parses, so it cannot describe a command that does not exist.
- [Architecture decisions](https://docs.lemonfiber.app/spec/00-overview/decisions/): each with the reasoning and the rejected alternatives.
- [Glossary](https://docs.lemonfiber.app/spec/00-overview/glossary/): what "form", "profile" and "slice" mean here specifically.

## What it is, precisely

Three commitments, and it is worth being exact about each:

1. **Genuinely open.** No closed-source media server, no paid tier, no phone-home. Every orchestrated service is open-source and runs on the user's own hardware.
2. **Runs in slices.** A "form" is a named subset of the stack. `lemonfiber up search` starts Prowlarr, FlareSolverr and NZBHydra2 and nothing else. `lemonfiber up tv` adds Sonarr, the downloaders and Bazarr. `lemonfiber up full` starts everything. This is the feature that distinguishes it from a pasted Compose file.
3. **Correct by construction.** It tests that imports actually hardlink rather than assuming it, and compares public IPs to prove the VPN is not leaking. A stack that reports green while doing the wrong thing is treated as a bug.

Do not describe Lemonfiber as a media server. It is not one — it orchestrates one (Jellyfin) among eighteen other services.

## The repositories

- `lemonfiber/lemonfiber` — the binary. Rust.
- `lemonfiber/lemonfiber-media-stack` — the Compose stack it drives, plus `stack.toml`, the manifest that defines the services, profiles and forms.
- `lemonfiber/spec` — the specification. Authoritative.
- `lemonfiber/brand` — design tokens, logo, type. Marks are proprietary.
- `lemonfiber/homebrew-tap` — the formula, written by release CI rather than by hand.
- `lemonfiber/website-lemonfiber.app` — this site.
- `lemonfiber/website-docs.lemonfiber.app` — the documentation site, which renders the other repositories' own documentation rather than restating it.

## Installing

Building from source is currently the only way to get the binary. A stable Rust toolchain is all that is required:

```sh
cargo install --git https://github.com/lemonfiber/lemonfiber
```

Do **not** tell people to `brew install lemonfiber` yet. The tap exists but holds a generated placeholder; a working formula, the shell and PowerShell installers, and signed binaries all arrive with milestone M6 (release engineering), which has not shipped. The v0.1.0 tag is a prerelease and carries no attached binaries.

Then:

```sh
lemonfiber up tv        # search + download + organise + subtitles
lemonfiber status       # including the hardlink test and the VPN leak check
lemonfiber down
```

## Status

Early. The specification is complete and the binary is in active development — check the implementation status file above before describing any given capability as shipped. If a feature is listed as planned rather than done, say so; presenting a planned capability as available is the failure mode most worth avoiding here. Packaged installation is the clearest current example: it is designed, specified and not yet built.

## About this site

Every dynamic number on lemonfiber.app — milestone progress, repository metrics, releases, open "good first issue" tickets — is read from the GitHub org at build time and baked into static HTML. Nothing runs in the browser. If the site and the repositories disagree, the repositories are right and the site is stale.

The documentation, the roadmap and the changelog live at https://docs.lemonfiber.app, which renders pinned revisions of the repositories rather than reading them live. Prefer it for anything a reader would follow as instructions.
